pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 🌐 **Strand 3 — Communication Networks**
Sub-strand 2: Internet and Social Media

Pictures and videos are the most shared content online. In this unit you will explore photo- and video-sharing platforms and strengthen your email skills with attachments and the address book.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**
- **B8.3.2.1** Demonstrate the use of social networking and electronic mail.

> 🧭 **What you will be able to do**
- **B8.3.2.1.1** Identify the various types of social media sites such as photo sharing (Instagram, Snapchat, Pinterest) and video sharing (YouTube, Facebook Live, Periscope, Vimeo); attach documents to email; use the address book.

> 🗺️ **Lessons in this unit**
- 9.1 Photo-Sharing and Video-Sharing Platforms

**Core competencies developed:** Communication and Collaboration, Digital Literacy (recognition of societal issues raised by digital technologies).

pages.title: Photo-Sharing and Video-Sharing Platforms
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.3.2.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- discuss photo-sharing sites;
- demonstrate video-sharing platforms;
- attach documents to email and use the address book.
## Photo-sharing sites
| **Platform** | **Main features** | **Example uses** |
|---|---|---|
| Instagram | Share photos and short videos (**Reels**) with filters and captions; **Stories** disappear after 24 hours; direct messages | Artists showcasing work; businesses advertising products |
| Snapchat | Photos and videos (“snaps”) that disappear after viewing; AR filters (lenses); Snap Map | Casual communication with friends |
| Pinterest | Save and organise images (“pins”) on themed boards; discover ideas | Craft, fashion, recipe and project ideas |
## Video-sharing sites
| **Platform** | **Main features** |
|---|---|
| YouTube | The largest video-sharing site: upload, watch, comment, subscribe; live streams; educational channels; YouTube Shorts |
| Facebook Live | Live video broadcasts to friends, pages and groups (used for church services, funerals, events, news) |
| Periscope | A live-streaming app owned by Twitter, **shut down in March 2021**; live video is now built into X |
| Vimeo | High-quality video hosting popular with film-makers and businesses; fewer adverts |
| TikTok | Short vertical videos with music and effects; very popular with young people |

pages.title: Photo-Sharing and Video-Sharing Platforms (continued)
pages.body:
> 🛡️ **Safety first — Sharing photos and videos responsibly**
- Never post photos that show your school uniform with your location, your house number, or other personal information.
- Ask permission before posting photos of other people.
- Turn off location tagging on photos.
- Remember: “disappearing” content can be screenshotted.
- Respect copyright: don’t upload other people’s music or films.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Demonstration: finding and saving a learning video on YouTube**
1. Open youtube.com and search for **“OSI model explained”**.
2. Check the channel’s credibility (views, subscribers, date) before watching.
3. Use **Settings (⚙)** to change quality or turn on **subtitles/CC**.
4. Click **Save** to add it to a playlist such as “B8 Computing”, or **Share › Copy link** to send it to your class group.
## Attaching a document to an email: review
> 🪜 **Step by step — Attaching files (Gmail or Outlook)**
1. Click **Compose** (Gmail) or **New mail** (Outlook).
2. Fill in **To**, **Subject** and the message.
3. Click the **paper-clip** icon (**Attach files**).
4. Browse to the file, select it (hold **Ctrl** to choose several) and click **Open**. You can also **drag and drop** the file into the message.
5. Wait for the upload bar to finish, check the file name, then click **Send**. Files above the size limit (25 MB in Gmail, 20 MB in Outlook.com) are sent as a cloud link (Google Drive / OneDrive).

pages.title: Using the address book
pages.body:
## Using the address book
Besides saving individual contacts, the address book lets you: **edit** and **delete** contacts; create **contact groups/labels** (e.g. “Computing Club”) and email the whole group by typing the group name; **import** contacts from a file or phone; and **search** quickly when composing.
> 💻 **Practical session**
Create a contact group of five classmates called B8 Project Team. Send the group an email with a ZIP file attachment containing your Unit 7 spreadsheet project, using **Bcc** to protect their addresses.
